description: security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm is extended directly rather than through config:best-practices, which also pulls in helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests, :configMigration, :pinDevDependencies, :maintainLockFilesWeekly, abandonments:recommended and docker:pinDigests. The first of those contradicts the convention that actions are pinned to exact release tags, which is shared across the kanso-labs repositories, and the rest are behaviours this repository has not opted into. Extending the security preset directly keeps its own null opt-outs for lockFileMaintenance, replacement, pin, bump, lockfileUpdate and rollback, which is what a hand-written top-level minimumReleaseAge would lose: those update types carry no release timestamp, so a global value raises pull requests that can never merge, and this repository automerges lockFileMaintenance.

packageRules.description: Renovate's own config:recommended sets semanticCommitType through a packageRule, and packageRules beat top-level config. Setting it at the top level therefore does nothing at all: every upgrade stays chore and cuts no release.

eslint-plugin-oxlint declares a hard `~` peer on the matching oxlint minor, so a lone bump of either resolves to ERESOLVE. The eslint rule above negates the plugin out of its `eslint-plugin-**` matcher so this pairing does not rest on rule order.

typescript-eslint peers typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0, and no published version admits 7 — the ceiling has moved 5.8, 5.9, 6.0, 6.1 and stopped there. So a TypeScript 7 branch fails Renovate's own lockfile update with ERESOLVE, leaves the lock stale, and every required check then dies at npm ci on "lock file's typescript@6.0.3 does not satisfy typescript@7.0.2". recreateWhen is always, so that pull request cannot be closed away. Lift this once typescript-eslint ships a peer range that admits 7; grouping the two cannot substitute, because no version of the group resolves.
